A management command's `--settings` option writes the same variable later, and unconditionally, so it wins over both: `ManagementUtility.execute` reads that option, and `handle_default_options` assigns its value (`django/core/management/base.py:handle_default_options`).

The module calls `get_wsgi_application` or `get_asgi_application`, and each of those is two lines: call `django.setup` with `set_prefix=False`, and return a new handler (`django/core/wsgi.py:get_wsgi_application`, `django/core/asgi.py:get_asgi_application`).

The module calls `get_wsgi_application` or `get_asgi_application`, and each of those is two lines: call `django.setup` with `set_prefix=False`, and return a new handler (`django/core/wsgi.py:get_wsgi_application`, `django/core/asgi.py:get_asgi_application`).

The argument tells `django.setup` to leave the script prefix alone, because under a server the handler sets it for each request, from `settings.FORCE_SCRIPT_NAME` or else from what the server passes with the request (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIHandler.__call__`).

Its constructor builds the middleware chain, which imports every middleware class and instantiates it, and some middleware modules import models, so the registry has to be ready first (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.load_middleware`).

`manage.py` and `django-admin` both end in `ManagementUtility.execute`, which calls `django.setup` before it has found the command's class (`django/core/management/__init__.py:ManagementUtility.execute`).

The reloader's first process starts a second, its child, running the same command, and starts it again each time the child exits on a change to a file (`django/utils/autoreload.py:restart_with_reloader`).

The failure is set aside, and the registry made to look populated with no applications, because the exception will be raised later, in the child process the reloader starts (`django/core/management/__init__.py:ManagementUtility.execute`).
`check_errors` notes the exception and the file it came from, and raises it again (`django/utils/autoreload.py:check_errors`).

With no application installed, the runserver to be found is the built-in one (`django/core/management/__init__.py:get_commands`), so `execute` takes off the command line any option that the built-in runserver does not know, those of the staticfiles application's runserver among them, and lets the command run.

Replacing `Apps.all_models` with an empty dictionary goes against the comment in `Apps.__init__`, which says the map is never replaced or reset (`django/apps/registry.py:Apps.__init__`); [The registry and its models](registry.md) gives the comment's reason.
`Apps.loading` left true does no harm, since `Apps.populate` returns before it looks at it once `Apps.ready` is true (`django/apps/registry.py:Apps.populate`).

When nothing is configured, `TemplateCommand.handle` gives the rendering settings of its own: it calls `settings.configure()` with no arguments, which yields the defaults alone, and then `django.setup`, which populates the registry with no applications (`django/core/management/templates.py:TemplateCommand.handle`).

A worker made any other way, spawned or forked from a separate fork server, has neither, and the function that initializes each worker calls `django.setup` for it (`django/test/runner.py:_init_worker`).

Called with no `INSTALLED_APPS`, it leaves the default, an empty list, and `django.setup` populates the registry with nothing, which is enough for the parts of Django that need settings and no installed application (`django/conf/__init__.py:LazySettings.configure`).

The development server makes one: the command has already started Django when it obtains the handler, and obtaining it runs `get_wsgi_application`, which calls `django.setup` again (`django/core/servers/basehttp.py:get_internal_wsgi_application`).

The second call finds the registry ready, and `Apps.populate` returns at once (`django/apps/registry.py:Apps.populate`), but it ordinarily configures logging again, and under a project's `LOGGING` that leaves out `"disable_existing_loggers"` a logger obtained between the two calls can be disabled ([Logging](logging.md)).
